I played all 24 months. All three training runs finished on time, every month's inference demand was fully served, and there were no penalties. The final **net cost is $1,351M**.

**Settlement ($M)**
| | |
|---|---|
| Spend | 1,615.4 (GPU purchases 1,250, power 291, cloud contracts 164.3, spot 11.9, minus 101.8 from reselling GPUs) |
| Value of GPUs still owned | −381.0 |
| Payments still owed after month 23 | +117.0 (mostly power contracts) |
| **Net cost** | **1,351.3** |

**Training runs**
| Window | Done | Needed |
|---|---|---|
| Months 0–7 | 173 | 60 |
| Months 8–15 | 380 | 140 |
| Months 16–23 | ~320 (315 before the last month) | 320 |

**What I did**
- **Early buying (months 0–2):** I ordered 50k gen H GPUs and signed 70 MW of power. Delivery was slow (about 6k a month at best), and the rumours pointed to gen N launching late, around month 18. So most capacity for the 320 kH-month final run had to come from gen H bought early.
- **Power for the final run:** I added 30 MW at month 7 so all the GPUs had power when the original 16 MW contract ended at month 19.
- **Extra capacity:** I reserved 10 kH of cloud capacity for months 16–21 at $1.125M per kH-month, and bought 10 kH of spot in month 17 when it was cheap ($0.78M).
- **Reselling:** I sold 6k GPUs in months 16–17, just before gen N cut used gen H prices by 40%, for about $81M. I sold another 3k in the final month.

**Where money was wasted**
- I bought far more than the first two runs needed (553 kH-months against 200). That was because GPUs had to be ordered early for the final run, so their output in the meantime went beyond what the earlier runs could use.
- The month-7 power contract started only at month 15, so most of its 24 months run past month 23. That is part of the $117M still owed.

**Final run margin:** it was closer than I'd normally accept. It finished with only about 25 kH-months to spare, because inference demand grew about 7% a month.
